_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Most people who played Metroid in 1986 never actually saw its most famous moment.

beats.lead: The manual gave it away, on purpose
beats.text: Samus Aran is called 'he' throughout Metroid's instruction manual, which also admits that little is known about 'him'.
beats.note: That was not a translation error. Nintendo built the disguise into the game's own paperwork.

beats.text: Metroid's ending depends on how long it takes to finish. Only the fastest clears show Samus without her suit at all.
beats.note: A first playthrough drawn out on paper by hand, the only option in 1986, realistically took five to ten hours. That ending does not remove her helmet.

beats.context: Clear the game inside that and the ending swaps Samus's armour for a bikini instead.

beats.name: Gunpei Yokoi
beats.role: Producer, working with director Satoru Okada, on a game that helped invent the exploration genre later named after it: the metroidvania.

beats.line: The ending you actually got depended entirely on how good you were at drawing your own map.
